purpose: Replace Python execution overhead with a native C++20 implementation of the already-tested BM6 numerical map, then replay the frozen primary Benchmark A contest.

native_lane.force_model: direct mutual unsoftened Newtonian point masses
native_lane.coefficient_precision: published decimal coefficients at approximately binary64 precision

reference_loose.method: SciPy DOP853 with independent math.fsum force implementation

reference_tight.method: SciPy DOP853 with independent math.fsum force implementation

gates.deterministic_replay: two native trajectory files must be byte-identical
gates.reference_gate: DOP853 loose-vs-tight RMS position and velocity disagreement must each be <=1% of the best competing error, using the existing absolute floors.
gates.accuracy_win_rule: All four all-body trajectory metrics must be lower than REBOUND and energy/angular-momentum gates must not worsen.
gates.timing_semantics: median integration-only timing; setup, diagnostics, trajectory output, and file I/O excluded

preservation: Do not modify the Python KDK, cached Yoshida-6, Python BM6, DE441 inputs, prior Benchmark A results, or equal-timestep verdict.
claim_ceiling: A scoped native replay and accuracy/speed comparison on the frozen smooth ten-body workload; not universal superiority over REBOUND, close-encounter validation, arbitrary-precision qualification, full ephemeris reconstruction, or a Planet-X claim.
